questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: Which activity does an IDE's run-time environment support?

questions.originalExplanation: It lets you run the program and inspect its behaviour or output.

questions.originalQuestion: How do IDE error diagnostics help?
questions.originalAnswer: They show errors and often their location, helping the programmer find the cause.
questions.originalExplanation: They show errors and often their location, helping the programmer find the cause.

questions.originalExplanation: The computers use different character sets or encodings. To show the same letter, both need a matching encoding.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: Convert 00101101 binary to denary.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: A character set maps characters to what?
questions.originalAnswer: A — Codes
questions.originalExplanation: A character set defines characters and the codes used to represent them.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “A record must contain only one unnamed value.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: Named fields about one item or person. Fields may have different data types.
questions.originalExplanation: Named fields about one item or person. Fields may have different data types.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: Valid ages are 13–18. Changing <18 to <=18 fixes a bug. Give three tests near 18 and their expected results. Why retest a value that worked before?

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: Why does 11111111 plus 00000001 overflow eight bits?
questions.originalAnswer: The true sum is 256, requiring nine bits; only eight stored bits would contain 00000000.
questions.originalExplanation: The true sum is 256, requiring nine bits; only eight stored bits would contain 00000000.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: A has code 65. Capital-letter codes go in order. What is D's code?
questions.originalExplanation: D is three places after A, so 65 + 3 = 68.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Unicode supports fewer characters than standard ASCII.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: Unicode supports far more characters than standard ASCII.
questions.originalExplanation: Unicode supports far more characters than standard ASCII.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A program calculates an area and shows a menu in several places. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) A function cannot return a value. (b) A procedure must return a value.
questions.originalAnswer: (a) A function returns a value, such as an area. (b) A procedure performs a task, such as showing a menu, without returning a value. Use arguments and return values to avoid unwanted changes to global data.
questions.originalExplanation: (a) A function returns a value, such as an area. (b) A procedure performs a task, such as showing a menu, without returning a value. Use arguments and return values to avoid unwanted changes to global data.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: Convert hexadecimal A3 to eight-bit binary.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: How many different codes can 7 bits represent?
questions.originalExplanation: There are 2^7 = 128 different patterns.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Metadata is another name for the colour of every pixel.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: Extra image details, such as width, height or colour depth. These are separate from pixel data.
questions.originalExplanation: Extra image details, such as width, height or colour depth. These are separate from pixel data.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: (a) A bitmap uses 5 bits per pixel. How many colours can it show? What if you add one bit? (b) A 50 × 20 pixel image doubles in width and height. Colour depth stays the same. How do pixel count and raw size change? Explain.
questions.originalAnswer: (a) 32 colours; one extra bit doubles this to 64. (b) 1,000 pixels become 4,000. Raw size is four times larger: both dimensions double.
questions.originalExplanation: (a) 32 colours; one extra bit doubles this to 64. (b) 1,000 pixels become 4,000. Raw size is four times larger: both dimensions double.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: How does a bitmap represent pixel colours?
questions.originalAnswer: Each pixel has a colour code stored in binary.
questions.originalExplanation: Each pixel has a colour code stored in binary.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: Virtual memory can slow programs because it uses slower ____.
questions.originalAnswer: D — Storage
questions.originalExplanation: Moving data between RAM and slower secondary storage adds delays.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “A parameter is the final printed output of every program.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: A named input received by a subprogram when called with an argument.
questions.originalExplanation: A named input received by a subprogram when called with an argument.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A microphone records digital sound. “Sampling stores every instant of the sound wave.” Correct this. How does it affect recorded detail?
questions.originalAnswer: Measure amplitude at regular intervals. Store each rounded (quantised) value in binary. Sample rate and bit depth limit the detail captured.
questions.originalExplanation: Measure amplitude at regular intervals. Store each rounded (quantised) value in binary. Sample rate and bit depth limit the detail captured.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: What does lossy compression do?
questions.originalAnswer: It discards some information, so the exact original cannot necessarily be restored.
questions.originalExplanation: It discards some information, so the exact original cannot necessarily be restored.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: RAM holds instructions and data currently being ____.
questions.originalAnswer: A — Used
questions.originalExplanation: RAM holds the program's working data and instructions. It is volatile.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Sample rate is the number of bits used for each sample.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: Sample rate is samples per second. At 8,000 Hz, 8,000 samples are taken each second. A higher rate can capture more detail but uses more space.
questions.originalExplanation: Sample rate is samples per second. At 8,000 Hz, 8,000 samples are taken each second. A higher rate can capture more detail but uses more space.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: Correct: 'Bit depth means samples per second.' If recordings differ only in bit depth, how do their quality and file size change?
questions.originalAnswer: Bit depth is bits per sample. More bits allow more amplitude levels but use more space. Longer duration adds samples; sample rate and bit depth control detail.
questions.originalExplanation: Bit depth is bits per sample. More bits allow more amplitude levels but use more space. Longer duration adds samples; sample rate and bit depth control detail.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: What is abstraction?
questions.originalAnswer: Removing irrelevant detail while keeping what is needed to solve the problem.
questions.originalExplanation: Removing irrelevant detail while keeping what is needed to solve the problem.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: Which action does WHERE perform in SQL?
questions.originalAnswer: B — Filters
questions.originalExplanation: WHERE keeps rows that meet the stated condition.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: A zero-indexed 2D array is [[11,12],[21,22]]. Give grid[1,0], then state the indexes needed to access 12.
questions.originalAnswer: grid[1,0] is 21; 12 is at grid[0,1].
questions.originalExplanation: grid[1,0] is 21; 12 is at grid[0,1].

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: Two mono recordings have the same sample rate and bit depth. One lasts twice as long. Does this double its quality? How does raw size change?
questions.originalAnswer: Raw size doubles: there are twice as many samples. Quality does not improve. Sample rate and bit depth stay the same.
questions.originalExplanation: Raw size doubles: there are twice as many samples. Quality does not improve. Sample rate and bit depth stay the same.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: What does a diamond represent in a flowchart?
questions.originalAnswer: A decision or condition with alternative paths.
questions.originalExplanation: A decision or condition with alternative paths.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: In OCR ERL, which value can random(1,6) return?
questions.originalExplanation: It can return any integer from 1 to 6, including both endpoints.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “A USB flash drive stores data on a rotating magnetic platter.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: Solid-state storage with no moving read/write mechanism.
questions.originalExplanation: Solid-state storage with no moving read/write mechanism.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A large file must cross a slow link. “Compression always makes files larger.” Correct this. How might compression affect transfer time?
questions.originalAnswer: A smaller file uses less storage and can be sent faster over the same link. Compression and decompression take processing time.
questions.originalExplanation: A smaller file uses less storage and can be sent faster over the same link. Compression and decompression take processing time.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: Why must a trace table follow executed assignments in order?
questions.originalAnswer: Each variable value depends on the state produced by earlier executed instructions.
questions.originalExplanation: Each variable value depends on the state produced by earlier executed instructions.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: Lossy compression permanently removes some original ____.
questions.originalAnswer: D — Information
questions.originalExplanation: Lossy compression discards information, so the exact original may not be restored.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Changing a variable name automatically fixes every logic error.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: Clear names show what values mean and help people read and change code.
questions.originalExplanation: Clear names show what values mean and help people read and change code.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A program is compressed before being sent. “Lossless compression removes source-code characters.” Correct this. Why does it matter here?
questions.originalAnswer: Lossless compression restores every character exactly. Losing characters could break the program. A thumbnail can lose some detail; source code cannot.
questions.originalExplanation: Lossless compression restores every character exactly. Losing characters could break the program. A thumbnail can lose some detail; source code cannot.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: Does linear search require a sorted list?
questions.originalAnswer: No; it examines items in sequence until a match is found or the list ends.
questions.originalExplanation: No; it examines items in sequence until a match is found or the list ends.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: Splitting a problem into smaller parts is called ____.
questions.originalAnswer: A — Decomposition
questions.originalExplanation: Break a large problem into smaller, manageable subproblems.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Every local variable can always be accessed directly from every other subprogram.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: A local variable can be used only within its own subprogram or local scope.
questions.originalExplanation: A local variable can be used only within its own subprogram or local scope.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: Several procedures share a global score. “A global variable can be read only in one subprogram.” Correct this. What risk does sharing it create?
questions.originalAnswer: Global variables can be used across the program. This risks unwanted changes and makes faults harder to trace. Use arguments and return values to avoid hidden changes.
questions.originalExplanation: Global variables can be used across the program. This risks unwanted changes and makes faults harder to trace. Use arguments and return values to avoid hidden changes.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: What must be true before binary search is used?
questions.originalAnswer: The list must be sorted. This lets the search safely rule out half the remaining items.
questions.originalExplanation: The list must be sorted. This lets the search safely rule out half the remaining items.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: What does the Memory Address Register hold?
questions.originalAnswer: B — Address
questions.originalExplanation: The Memory Address Register holds the address of the memory location being accessed.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Functions can return only one digit and can never return an array.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: Yes. A subprogram can receive an array; a function can return an array.
questions.originalExplanation: Yes. A subprogram can receive an array; a function can return an array.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A café program finds the cost of identical drinks. “Inputs are the final results.” Correct this. Give the inputs, process and output.
questions.originalAnswer: Inputs: price and quantity. Processing: multiply them. Output: total cost. Inputs come before the calculation; the output comes after it.
questions.originalExplanation: Inputs: price and quantity. Processing: multiply them. Output: total cost. Inputs come before the calculation; the output comes after it.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: When does ascending bubble sort swap two adjacent items?
questions.originalAnswer: When the left item is greater than the right item.
questions.originalExplanation: When the left item is greater than the right item.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: What does readLine() do with the next line of a file?
questions.originalAnswer: C — Reads
questions.originalExplanation: It reads the next line and advances the current file position.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Primary storage exists only to keep long-term backups.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: It holds instructions and working data that the CPU needs while programs run.
questions.originalExplanation: It holds instructions and working data that the CPU needs while programs run.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: “My unsaved work will survive a power cut because this computer has ROM.” Explain the mistake. How could the work have been kept?
questions.originalAnswer: Unsaved work is in volatile RAM, so it is lost when power goes off. Save it to non-volatile secondary storage to keep it.
questions.originalExplanation: Unsaved work is in volatile RAM, so it is lost when power goes off. Save it to non-volatile secondary storage to keep it.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: What does insertion sort do with the next unsorted item?
questions.originalAnswer: Place the next item in the correct position in the sorted part. Shift larger items right.
questions.originalExplanation: Place the next item in the correct position in the sorted part. Shift larger items right.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: ROM commonly stores startup ____.
questions.originalAnswer: D — Firmware
questions.originalExplanation: ROM keeps firmware or startup instructions when power is off.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Cache is a remote Internet server that replaces CPU registers.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: Cache is in or near the CPU. It gives faster access to often-used data and instructions than main memory.
questions.originalExplanation: Cache is in or near the CPU. It gives faster access to often-used data and instructions than main memory.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A pupil restarts a computer to open saved work. “RAM keeps every file forever.” Correct this. Why is secondary storage needed?
questions.originalAnswer: Secondary storage keeps files and programs without power. Save the work there before restarting.
questions.originalExplanation: Secondary storage keeps files and programs without power. Save the work there before restarting.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: How does merge sort combine two sorted lists?
questions.originalAnswer: Compare the next item in each list. Take the smaller. Repeat, then add any items left over.
questions.originalExplanation: Compare the next item in each list. Take the smaller. Repeat, then add any items left over.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: What storage technology does a DVD use?
questions.originalAnswer: A — Optical
questions.originalExplanation: A DVD is optical storage, read using laser light.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “FROM is the clause that specifies the required output columns.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: The table to get data from.
questions.originalExplanation: The table to get data from.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A programmer writes print("Hello" and receives a syntax error. Identify the error and explain why the statement cannot run correctly.
questions.originalAnswer: The closing bracket ) is missing. This breaks the language's syntax rules. Add the bracket so the statement becomes print("Hello").
questions.originalExplanation: The closing bracket ) is missing. This breaks the language's syntax rules. Add the bracket so the statement becomes print("Hello").

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: Which CPU component performs arithmetic and logical operations?
questions.originalAnswer: The ALU performs arithmetic and logical operations.
questions.originalExplanation: The ALU performs arithmetic and logical operations.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: Which advantage makes HDDs suitable for large archives?
questions.originalAnswer: B — Cost
questions.originalExplanation: An HDD can provide lots of storage at a low cost per GB.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “An SSD is faster because its magnetic read head rotates more quickly.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: It does not need a moving head to seek positions on spinning platters.
questions.originalExplanation: It does not need a moving head to seek positions on spinning platters.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A laptop is used on a bumpy bus. “Portability and durability mean the same thing.” Correct this. How should this affect the storage choice?
questions.originalAnswer: Durability means resisting damage; portability means being easy to carry. An SSD has no moving read/write parts, so it handles shocks better. Size and weight also matter.
questions.originalExplanation: Durability means resisting damage; portability means being easy to carry. An SSD has no moving read/write parts, so it handles shocks better. Size and weight also matter.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: For s = 'COMPUTER', what is s.substring(1,3) in OCR ERL?
questions.originalAnswer: OMP; indexing starts at zero and the second argument gives length.
questions.originalExplanation: OMP; indexing starts at zero and the second argument gives length.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: Which could be the output of a greeting program?
questions.originalAnswer: C — Greeting
questions.originalExplanation: The displayed greeting is produced by the program. The other actions supply input.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Duplicating the same long code block everywhere always improves maintainability.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: Related logic can be reused, understood, tested and changed in one place.
questions.originalExplanation: Related logic can be reused, understood, tested and changed in one place.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: Nested IF statements are hard to read. “Indentation proves the logic is correct.” Correct this. How does indentation help?
questions.originalAnswer: Indentation shows blocks and nesting. Some languages require it. It helps people read and change code, but does not prove the logic is correct.
questions.originalExplanation: Indentation shows blocks and nesting. Some languages require it. It helps people read and change code, but does not prove the logic is correct.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: How is a cell selected in a two-dimensional array?
questions.originalAnswer: Use two indexes: one for the row and one for the column.
questions.originalExplanation: Use two indexes: one for the row and one for the column.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: A useful code comment should explain its ____.
questions.originalAnswer: D — Purpose
questions.originalExplanation: Useful comments explain intent or reasoning to help others understand the code.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “The CPU's main purpose is permanent file storage.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: It executes instructions to process data.
questions.originalExplanation: It executes instructions to process data.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A folder contains 20 images of 200 KB each. Using decimal units, give its total size in KB and MB.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: What is the scope of a local variable or constant?
questions.originalAnswer: A local variable can be used only within its own subprogram or local scope.
questions.originalExplanation: A local variable can be used only within its own subprogram or local scope.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: What does the CPU retrieve during the fetch stage?
questions.originalAnswer: A — Instruction
questions.originalExplanation: The CPU gets the next instruction from memory.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Execution only copies an instruction into memory without performing it.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: The operation specified by the decoded instruction is carried out.
questions.originalExplanation: The operation specified by the decoded instruction is carried out.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: “The Control Unit stores your documents forever.” Correct this. Explain its role when the CPU runs an instruction.
questions.originalAnswer: The Control Unit decodes instructions and controls CPU operations. The ALU processes data; registers store it briefly.
questions.originalExplanation: The Control Unit decodes instructions and controls CPU operations. The ALU processes data; registers store it briefly.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: Why open a file before reading it?
questions.originalAnswer: Opening establishes a handle or connection through which the program accesses the file.
questions.originalExplanation: Opening establishes a handle or connection through which the program accesses the file.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: CPU cache holds frequently used instructions and ____.
questions.originalAnswer: B — Data
questions.originalExplanation: Cache holds frequently or recently used data and instructions for fast access.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “A register is a large external drive used for backups.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: A small, fast storage location inside the CPU. It holds data or addresses in use.
questions.originalExplanation: A small, fast storage location inside the CPU. It holds data or addresses in use.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: The next instruction is at address 240. An addition gives 18. What do the accumulator and Program Counter hold? Explain the difference.
questions.originalAnswer: The accumulator holds the result, 18. The PC holds the next instruction's address, 240.
questions.originalExplanation: The accumulator holds the result, 18. The PC holds the next instruction's address, 240.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: What does SELECT specify in an SQL query?
questions.originalAnswer: The fields (columns) to return.
questions.originalExplanation: The fields (columns) to return.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: A higher CPU clock speed means more ____ per second.
questions.originalAnswer: C — Cycles
questions.originalExplanation: Clock speed measures CPU clock cycles per second.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Larger cache increases the number of installed CPU cores.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: A larger cache holds more often-used data and instructions. This can reduce slower memory access.
questions.originalExplanation: A larger cache holds more often-used data and instructions. This can reduce slower memory access.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: CPU A: 4 GHz, two cores, 2 MB cache. CPU B: 3 GHz, eight cores, 8 MB cache. Why is neither fastest for every task?
questions.originalAnswer: A has more cycles per second, which may help one task. B has more cores for parallel work and more cache to reduce slow memory access. Speed also depends on the task and CPU design.
questions.originalExplanation: A has more cycles per second, which may help one task. B has more cores for parallel work and more cache to reduce slow memory access. Speed also depends on the task and CPU design.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: Which integers can random(1,6) produce in OCR ERL?
questions.originalAnswer: Any integer from 1 through 6 inclusive.
questions.originalExplanation: Any integer from 1 through 6 inclusive.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: Why might a programmer write pseudocode first?
questions.originalAnswer: D — Planning
questions.originalExplanation: Pseudocode describes algorithm steps without needing one language's exact syntax.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “A diamond is used only for unconditional calculations.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: A decision or condition with alternative paths.
questions.originalExplanation: A decision or condition with alternative paths.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A program works out a bill, then applies a discount. “The order of steps never matters.” Correct this. What could go wrong?
questions.originalAnswer: Steps must be clear and in the right order. Check that conditions give the right result for every allowed input.
questions.originalExplanation: Steps must be clear and in the right order. Check that conditions give the right result for every allowed input.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: In a trace table, should you record executed variable updates or only variable names?
questions.originalAnswer: Executed variable updates in their actual order.
questions.originalExplanation: Executed variable updates in their actual order.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: A triangle with a small output bubble represents which gate?
questions.originalAnswer: A — NOT

questions.originalQuestion: An indicator uses Q = NOT A. Give outputs for A=0 and A=1, then evaluate NOT(NOT A) for both values.
questions.originalAnswer: Q: 1, 0. Double NOT: 0, 1, restoring A.

questions.originalExplanation: (a) [7, 2]; 2 comparison(s), found at index 1.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: After correcting an assessment answer, why attempt a new question?
questions.originalAnswer: To check that the method can be applied independently rather than copied.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: After one ascending bubble-sort pass on [7, 3, 6, 2], what is the list?

questions.originalExplanation: Whether a user has supplied suitable evidence of the claimed identity.

questions.originalQuestion: High-level code must become what for the CPU to execute it?
questions.originalAnswer: C — Machine code

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Sequence means the computer chooses any random instruction order.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: Instructions execute in the specified order.
questions.originalExplanation: Instructions execute in the specified order.

questions.originalQuestion: What does anticipating misuse mean in defensive design?
questions.originalAnswer: Planning for invalid, unexpected or malicious use and handling it safely.
questions.originalExplanation: Planning for invalid, unexpected or malicious use and handling it safely.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ

questions.originalQuestion: “A comparison operator must always produce a text paragraph.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: A Boolean result: true or false.
questions.originalExplanation: A Boolean result: true or false.

questions.originalQuestion: A school shares files and printers on one site. “A LAN must span several countries.” Correct this. Why does a LAN fit here?

questions.originalExplanation: A LAN connects devices in a small area, such as one school site. A WAN links networks over a large area. Internet access alone does not make a LAN a WAN.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: For valid ages 13–18, identify the two valid boundary values.
questions.originalAnswer: 13 and 18 lie on the edges of the valid range.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A warning needs high temperature OR high pressure. “OR is false when both inputs are true.” Correct this. What happens when both are high?
questions.originalAnswer: OR is true if at least one input is true, including both. AND needs both true. NOT reverses a value.
questions.originalExplanation: OR is true if at least one input is true, including both. AND needs both true. NOT reverses a value.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: What does assignment do to a variable?
questions.originalAnswer: It stores a value in the named variable, replacing its previous value if one existed.
questions.originalExplanation: It stores a value in the named variable, replacing its previous value if one existed.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: In Boolean logic, NOT true evaluates to ____.
questions.originalAnswer: C — false
questions.originalExplanation: NOT reverses a Boolean value: true becomes false.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: What values does a Boolean variable represent?
questions.originalAnswer: True or false.
questions.originalExplanation: True or false.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: Computers share files on one school site. Two sites in different towns also need a link. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) A LAN spans several countries. (b) A WAN only works in one room.
questions.originalAnswer: (a) A LAN covers a small area, such as a school site. (b) A WAN links networks over a large area, often using outside providers' links. Internet access alone does not decide the type.
questions.originalExplanation: (a) A LAN covers a small area, such as a school site. (b) A WAN links networks over a large area, often using outside providers' links. Internet access alone does not decide the type.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: What is the result of concatenating 'AB' and '12'?
questions.originalAnswer: AB12, with no automatically inserted space.
questions.originalExplanation: AB12, with no automatically inserted space.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: What identifies an element's position in an array?
questions.originalAnswer: D — Index
questions.originalExplanation: Each array element has an index. OCR ERL indexes start at 0.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Testing a few inputs proves a program can never contain any fault.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: To identify faults and check behaviour against requirements using expected results.
questions.originalExplanation: To identify faults and check behaviour against requirements using expected results.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: Correct and explain: (a) Iterative testing starts only after delivery. (b) Final testing makes testing during development unnecessary.
questions.originalAnswer: (a) Iterative testing checks and fixes parts while building the program. (b) Final testing checks the finished program against its requirements. Both are needed.
questions.originalExplanation: (a) Iterative testing checks and fixes parts while building the program. (b) Final testing checks the finished program against its requirements. Both are needed.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: What does input validation check?
questions.originalAnswer: Whether input meets specified rules; it does not prove factual truth or identity.
questions.originalExplanation: Whether input meets specified rules; it does not prove factual truth or identity.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: Valid ages are integers from 13 to 18. Which input has the right type but is invalid?
questions.originalExplanation: 12 is an integer, but it is outside the valid range.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Defensive design assumes every user always enters valid and harmless data.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: Planning for invalid, unexpected or malicious use and handling it safely.
questions.originalExplanation: Planning for invalid, unexpected or malicious use and handling it safely.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A desktop needs a LAN connection. “A NIC keeps files when power is off.” Correct this. What does a NIC do here?
questions.originalAnswer: A NIC lets a device connect to a network. It has a different job from storage or a router.
questions.originalExplanation: A NIC lets a device connect to a network. It has a different job from storage or a router.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: What is a one-dimensional array?
questions.originalAnswer: A fixed-size indexed collection of related elements; OCR ERL indexing begins at zero.
questions.originalExplanation: A fixed-size indexed collection of related elements; OCR ERL indexing begins at zero.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: Valid ages are 13–18. Which is normal test data?
questions.originalExplanation: 15 is an ordinary valid age, away from the boundaries.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Any device connected to the Internet is automatically an embedded system.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: It is part of a heating system, with the specific task of controlling temperature.
questions.originalExplanation: It is part of a heating system, with the specific task of controlling temperature.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A pupil enters a domain name. “DNS gives the same MAC address to every visitor.” Correct this. How does DNS help find the website?
questions.originalAnswer: DNS servers look up the IP address for a domain name. Access needs the relevant server and network services to work.
questions.originalExplanation: DNS servers look up the IP address for a domain name. Access needs the relevant server and network services to work.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: How can a loop total an array's values?
questions.originalAnswer: Set a total to 0. Loop through the array, adding each value once.
questions.originalExplanation: Set a total to 0. Loop through the array, adding each value once.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: An embedded system is designed for a ____ task.
questions.originalAnswer: C — Specific
questions.originalExplanation: An embedded system performs a specific task within a larger device.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Adding active users always increases the bandwidth available to each user.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: Users may compete for finite bandwidth, reducing the data rate available to each.
questions.originalExplanation: Users may compete for finite bandwidth, reducing the data rate available to each.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A school uses client-server; club laptops share peer-to-peer. Correct and explain: (a) Every client is a server. (b) Peer-to-peer requires a central server.
questions.originalAnswer: (a) A server manages shared services and resources for clients. (b) Peers share directly and can act as clients and servers. Central control suits a school; peer-to-peer can cost less for a small club but is harder to manage as it grows.
questions.originalExplanation: (a) A server manages shared services and resources for clients. (b) Peers share directly and can act as clients and servers. Central control suits a school; peer-to-peer can cost less for a small club but is harder to manage as it grows.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: How is a cell selected in a two-dimensional array?
questions.originalAnswer: Use two indexes: one for the row and one for the column.
questions.originalExplanation: Use two indexes: one for the row and one for the column.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: A router connects different ____.
questions.originalAnswer: D — Networks
questions.originalExplanation: Routers forward data between networks using IP addresses.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “An IPv4 address is always six pairs of hexadecimal digits separated by colons.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: IPv4 supports addressing and routing. It is usually written as four decimal numbers separated by dots.
questions.originalExplanation: IPv4 supports addressing and routing. It is usually written as four decimal numbers separated by dots.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: Tablets need to join a wired LAN. “A WAP changes domain names into IP addresses.” Correct this. How does a WAP help the tablets?
questions.originalAnswer: A wireless access point connects wireless devices to a network. It has a different job from a switch or router.
questions.originalExplanation: A wireless access point connects wireless devices to a network. It has a different job from a switch or router.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: What is a record?
questions.originalAnswer: Named fields about one item or person. Fields may have different data types.
questions.originalExplanation: Named fields about one item or person. Fields may have different data types.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: Retesting after a fix can detect newly introduced ____.
questions.originalAnswer: A — Faults
questions.originalExplanation: Check the fix and make sure previously working features still work.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “The Internet is a single computer containing every website.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: A worldwide collection of interconnected computer networks.
questions.originalExplanation: A worldwide collection of interconnected computer networks.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A browser asks for a school's web page. “A client must host a website before asking for it.” Correct this. Which computer provides the page?
questions.originalAnswer: A web server stores website resources and sends them when clients request them. Access needs working servers and network services.
questions.originalExplanation: A web server stores website resources and sends them when clients request them. Access needs working servers and network services.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: What distinguishes a function from a procedure?
questions.originalAnswer: A function returns a value to the caller. A procedure performs a task without returning a function value.
questions.originalExplanation: A function returns a value to the caller. A procedure performs a task without returning a function value.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: SMTP sends what type of message?
questions.originalAnswer: B — Email
questions.originalExplanation: SMTP sends email from clients to servers and between mail servers.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Cloud storage guarantees that files remain accessible during every Internet outage.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: Storage, software or processing on remote servers, accessed over a network. Access depends on the connection and service.
questions.originalExplanation: Storage, software or processing on remote servers, accessed over a network. Access depends on the connection and service.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A school buys network devices from different makers. “Standards mean all devices must have the same maker.” Correct this. How do standards help?
questions.originalAnswer: Agreed standards let hardware and software from different makers work together and exchange data.
questions.originalExplanation: Agreed standards let hardware and software from different makers work together and exchange data.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: When might a procedure be suitable?
questions.originalAnswer: For a named reusable task such as displaying a menu when no function result is required.
questions.originalExplanation: For a named reusable task such as displaying a menu when no function result is required.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: In OCR ERL, s = 'VARIABLE'. What is s.substring(1,3)?
questions.originalAnswer: C — ARI
questions.originalExplanation: Indexes start at 0. Start at index 1 and take 3 characters.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Failure of any one workstation cable necessarily disables all other star-network links.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: If the central switch fails, devices using it lose contact. A broken cable usually affects just one workstation.
questions.originalExplanation: If the central switch fails, devices using it lose contact. A broken cable usually affects just one workstation.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A network must cope if one link fails. “A mesh has only one path between any two devices.” Correct this. How could it keep working?
questions.originalAnswer: A mesh has other paths if some links fail. More links add cost and complexity. Check the paths that remain.
questions.originalExplanation: A mesh has other paths if some links fail. More links add cost and complexity. Check the paths that remain.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: What is a parameter?
questions.originalAnswer: A named input received by a subprogram when called with an argument.
questions.originalExplanation: A named input received by a subprogram when called with an argument.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: Phishing messages pretend to come from a ____ source.
questions.originalAnswer: D — Trusted
questions.originalExplanation: A fake trusted message tricks someone into revealing data or taking an unsafe action.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Fibre carries electrical signals through copper wire.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: Fibre uses light. It supports fast data transfer over long distances and resists electromagnetic interference. Installation can cost more.
questions.originalExplanation: Fibre uses light. It supports fast data transfer over long distances and resists electromagnetic interference. Installation can cost more.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: Desktops and moving tablets need network links. “Wi-Fi needs a cable from each tablet to the switch.” Correct this. Which links suit these devices?
questions.originalAnswer: Ethernet uses cables. Wi-Fi uses radio, so tablets can move around, but interference can affect it. Choose links to suit the distance and data rate needed.
questions.originalExplanation: Ethernet uses cables. Wi-Fi uses radio, so tablets can move around, but interference can affect it. Choose links to suit the distance and data rate needed.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: Why close a file after use?
questions.originalAnswer: It releases the handle or resources and helps ensure buffered writes are completed.
questions.originalExplanation: It releases the handle or resources and helps ensure buffered writes are completed.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: Which nearby device is commonly connected using Bluetooth?
questions.originalAnswer: A — Keyboard
questions.originalExplanation: Bluetooth suits short-range wireless links with modest data needs.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Brute force works only by physically breaking the computer.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: It tries many possible passwords or keys until one works.
questions.originalExplanation: It tries many possible passwords or keys until one works.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A network shows 2001:db8::7. “IPv6 uses four decimal numbers separated by dots.” Correct this. How is this address written?
questions.originalAnswer: IPv6 uses hexadecimal groups separated by colons. Groups of zeros can be shortened. Routers use IP addresses between networks; switches use MAC addresses within a LAN.
questions.originalExplanation: IPv6 uses hexadecimal groups separated by colons. Groups of zeros can be shortened. Routers use IP addresses between networks; switches use MAC addresses within a LAN.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: What does WHERE do in an SQL query?
questions.originalAnswer: It selects rows that meet a condition.
questions.originalExplanation: It selects rows that meet a condition.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: A MAC address identifies a network ____.
questions.originalAnswer: B — Interface
questions.originalExplanation: A MAC address identifies a network interface for local network communication.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “A firewall confirms that every sentence on every website is true.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: It uses rules to allow or block network traffic.
questions.originalExplanation: It uses rules to allow or block network traffic.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: Data must reach another network in the right order. “TCP chooses fonts; IP draws images.” Correct this. Explain each protocol's job.
questions.originalAnswer: TCP supports reliable delivery in order. IP handles addressing and routing between networks. Each protocol has its own job; encryption does not prove a site is honest.
questions.originalExplanation: TCP supports reliable delivery in order. IP handles addressing and routing between networks. Each protocol has its own job; encryption does not prove a site is honest.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: Which integers can random(1,6) produce in OCR ERL?
questions.originalAnswer: Any integer from 1 through 6 inclusive.
questions.originalExplanation: Any integer from 1 through 6 inclusive.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: HTTP is mainly used to transfer ____.
questions.originalAnswer: C — Webpages
questions.originalExplanation: HTTP transfers resources between web clients and servers.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Penetration testing permits anyone to attack any network without permission.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: Testing with permission, within agreed limits, to find and fix security weaknesses.
questions.originalExplanation: Testing with permission, within agreed limits, to find and fix security weaknesses.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A zero-indexed 2D array is [[11,12],[21,22]]. Give grid[1,0], then state the indexes needed to access 12.
questions.originalAnswer: (a) grid[1,0] is 21; 12 is at grid[0,1].
questions.originalExplanation: (a) grid[1,0] is 21; 12 is at grid[0,1].

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: What does authentication establish?
questions.originalAnswer: Whether a user has supplied suitable evidence of the claimed identity.
questions.originalExplanation: Whether a user has supplied suitable evidence of the claimed identity.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: Which protocol downloads messages from an email server?
questions.originalAnswer: D — POP
questions.originalExplanation: POP retrieves email from a mail server to a client.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Changing one protocol layer always requires every other layer to be redesigned.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: Layers split communication into tasks. They provide services to each other and help compatibility, development and finding faults.
questions.originalExplanation: Layers split communication into tasks. They provide services to each other and help compatibility, development and finding faults.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A drive with private records is lost. “Encryption stops files being stolen or deleted.” Correct this. What does it protect?
questions.originalAnswer: Without the key, an attacker cannot easily read ciphertext. Encryption does not stop theft or deletion. Use other controls for other threats.
questions.originalExplanation: Without the key, an attacker cannot easily read ciphertext. Encryption does not stop theft or deletion. Use other controls for other threats.

077.title: Testing: Normal, Boundary and Invalid Data

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: Why use meaningful variable names?
questions.originalAnswer: Clear names show what values mean and help people read and change code.
questions.originalExplanation: Clear names show what values mean and help people read and change code.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: FTP is primarily used to transfer ____.
questions.originalAnswer: A — Files
questions.originalExplanation: FTP transfers files between networked computers.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Malware means any program that uses a large amount of RAM.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: Malware is made to cause harm, disruption or access without permission. Different types work in different ways.
questions.originalExplanation: Malware is made to cause harm, disruption or access without permission. Different types work in different ways.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A school website is flooded with requests. “A denial-of-service attack makes access better for real users.” Correct this. What happens to them?
questions.originalAnswer: A denial-of-service attack floods a service with traffic or requests. Genuine users then cannot use it.
questions.originalExplanation: A denial-of-service attack floods a service with traffic or requests. Genuine users then cannot use it.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: For valid ages 13–18, give an ordinary normal test value.
questions.originalAnswer: 15 is a representative valid value away from the boundaries.
questions.originalExplanation: 15 is a representative valid value away from the boundaries.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: A local variable can be accessed within which scope?
questions.originalAnswer: B — Local
questions.originalExplanation: A local variable is accessible only within its defining scope.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Data interception is only copying a paper document from a filing cabinet.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: Capturing data during transmission, potentially exposing confidential information.
questions.originalExplanation: Capturing data during transmission, potentially exposing confidential information.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A new user needs to open and sort files. “A user interface replaces all CPU instructions.” Correct this. How does an interface help?
questions.originalAnswer: A user interface lets people use the computer, through GUI controls or typed commands. Other OS tasks manage devices, accounts, memory and files.
questions.originalExplanation: A user interface lets people use the computer, through GUI controls or typed commands. Other OS tasks manage devices, accounts, memory and files.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: What is the purpose of testing a program against expected outputs?
questions.originalAnswer: To compare its actual behaviour with the requirements and identify faults.
questions.originalExplanation: To compare its actual behaviour with the requirements and identify faults.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: SQL injection can manipulate a database ____.
questions.originalAnswer: C — Query
questions.originalExplanation: SQL injection lets unsafe input alter a query and may expose or change data.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: Can an array be passed to or returned from a subprogram?
questions.originalAnswer: Yes. A subprogram can receive an array; a function can return an array.
questions.originalExplanation: Yes. A subprogram can receive an array; a function can return an array.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A school updates its anti-malware. “Anti-malware can detect every future threat.” Correct this. Why are other controls needed?
questions.originalAnswer: Anti-malware detects, quarantines or removes malware. Updates help it recognise threats. It cannot stop every attack, so other controls are needed.
questions.originalExplanation: Anti-malware detects, quarantines or removes malware. Updates help it recognise threats. It cannot stop every attack, so other controls are needed.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: Name one useful item to record when correcting a failed test.
questions.originalAnswer: The input, expected output, actual output or identified fault, with the correction.
questions.originalExplanation: The input, expected output, actual output or identified fault, with the correction.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: Users should be given only ____ access rights.
questions.originalAnswer: D — Necessary
questions.originalExplanation: Limited permissions reduce unwanted access and damage.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “A printer driver stores only the user's website passwords.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: It enables communication with and control of a particular peripheral.
questions.originalExplanation: It enables communication with and control of a particular peripheral.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A program reads names then saves results. Correct and explain: (a) readLine() writes a line. (b) writeLine(text) only displays text.
questions.originalAnswer: (a) readLine() reads the next line and moves forward. (b) writeLine(text) writes a line to an open file. Open, read or write, then close. Screen output does not save a file.
questions.originalExplanation: (a) readLine() reads the next line and moves forward. (b) writeLine(text) writes a line to an open file. Open, read or write, then close. Screen output does not save a file.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: Why must a trace table follow executed assignments in order?
questions.originalAnswer: Each variable value depends on the state produced by earlier executed instructions.
questions.originalExplanation: Each variable value depends on the state produced by earlier executed instructions.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: Opening a file creates a file ____ for access.
questions.originalAnswer: A — Handle
questions.originalExplanation: Opening a file sets up a handle through which the program accesses it.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Reusing one short password everywhere improves account security.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: They make guessing harder and prevent reuse of a compromised password across accounts.
questions.originalExplanation: They make guessing harder and prevent reuse of a compromised password across accounts.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A file is split into fragments on an HDD. “Defragmentation speeds up every SSD by moving its read head.” Correct this. When does defragmentation help?
questions.originalAnswer: Defragmentation brings file fragments together on an HDD, reducing read-head movement. It rearranges data; it does not encrypt or compress it.
questions.originalExplanation: Defragmentation brings file fragments together on an HDD, reducing read-head movement. It rearranges data; it does not encrypt or compress it.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: What is a syntax error?
questions.originalAnswer: A syntax error breaks the language's rules. The affected code cannot be translated or run correctly.
questions.originalExplanation: A syntax error breaks the language's rules. The affected code cannot be translated or run correctly.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: What does FROM identify in an SQL SELECT statement?
questions.originalAnswer: B — Table
questions.originalExplanation: FROM specifies the table from which data is retrieved.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Encryption prevents all network packets from being intercepted.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: Encryption changes plaintext into ciphertext. Someone who intercepts it cannot easily read it without the key.
questions.originalExplanation: Encryption changes plaintext into ciphertext. Someone who intercepts it cannot easily read it without the key.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A school replaces working laptops each year. “This has no environmental cost.” Correct this. What resources or waste are involved?
questions.originalAnswer: Making devices uses energy and raw materials. Disposal adds electronic waste. Consider who benefits and who is harmed.
questions.originalExplanation: Making devices uses energy and raw materials. Disposal adds electronic waste. Consider who benefits and who is harmed.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: Does linear search require a sorted list?
questions.originalAnswer: No; it examines items in sequence until a match is found or the list ends.
questions.originalExplanation: No; it examines items in sequence until a match is found or the list ends.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: Which is a physical rather than software security measure?
questions.originalAnswer: C — Lock
questions.originalExplanation: A locked room limits physical access and reduces theft or tampering.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “The Data Protection Act permits unlimited retention and sharing of all pupil data.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: It sets rules for using personal data lawfully and protects people's rights.
questions.originalExplanation: It sets rules for using personal data lawfully and protects people's rights.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A pupil opens another pupil's account without permission but changes nothing. “Access is legal if no files are deleted.” Correct this. Why could it still break the law?
questions.originalAnswer: Access without permission can break the Computer Misuse Act, even if no files change. A law or licence sets what is allowed; having a copy does not give unlimited rights.
questions.originalExplanation: Access without permission can break the Computer Misuse Act, even if no files change. A law or licence sets what is allowed; having a copy does not give unlimited rights.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: What must be true before binary search is used?
questions.originalAnswer: The list must be sorted. This lets the search safely rule out half the remaining items.
questions.originalExplanation: The list must be sorted. This lets the search safely rule out half the remaining items.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: A shared subprogram lets you change common logic how many times?
questions.originalAnswer: D — Once
questions.originalExplanation: Reusable code can be changed and tested in one place.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: Why is indentation useful?
questions.originalAnswer: Indentation shows blocks and nesting clearly. Some languages require it.
questions.originalExplanation: Indentation shows blocks and nesting clearly. Some languages require it.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: Correct: 'A comment changes the next variable's value.' How could comments help when a validation rule changes next year?
questions.originalAnswer: A comment explains why code works or what it is for. Clear comments help others understand and change it.
questions.originalExplanation: A comment explains why code works or what it is for. Clear comments help others understand and change it.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: When does ascending bubble sort swap two adjacent items?
questions.originalAnswer: When the left item is greater than the right item.
questions.originalExplanation: When the left item is greater than the right item.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: An OS supports multitasking by sharing processor ____.
questions.originalAnswer: A — Time
questions.originalExplanation: The OS shares processor time and manages memory for running applications.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “Open source means there are never any licence conditions or costs.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: It permits access to source code and modification or redistribution under its conditions.
questions.originalExplanation: It permits access to source code and modification or redistribution under its conditions.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A school uses biased software; a business shares licensed code. Correct and explain: (a) Legal always means ethical. (b) Law depends only on popularity.
questions.originalAnswer: (a) Ethics concerns fairness, responsibility and what is right. (b) Law sets what is allowed or banned. Consider effects on people: a legal action may still be unfair or intrusive.
questions.originalExplanation: (a) Ethics concerns fairness, responsibility and what is right. (b) Law sets what is allowed or banned. Consider effects on people: a legal action may still be unfair or intrusive.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
questions.originalQuestion: What does insertion sort do with the next unsorted item?
questions.originalAnswer: Place the next item in the correct position in the sorted part. Shift larger items right.
questions.originalExplanation: Place the next item in the correct position in the sorted part. Shift larger items right.

questions.label: Earlier learning — MCQ
questions.originalQuestion: Which activity suits utility software?
questions.originalAnswer: B — Maintenance
questions.originalExplanation: Utilities perform maintenance, protection and other housekeeping tasks.

questions.label: Earlier learning
questions.originalQuestion: “File management is only the execution of arithmetic instructions.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.originalAnswer: It manages files and folders: naming, saving, copying, moving and deleting them.
questions.originalExplanation: It manages files and folders: naming, saving, copying, moving and deleting them.

questions.label: Prior learning — challenge
questions.originalQuestion: A teacher stores private records on a portable drive. “An encryption utility makes a drive weigh less.” Correct this. What does it protect?
questions.originalAnswer: Encryption uses an algorithm and key to change readable data into ciphertext. It protects privacy; compression reduces size and defragmentation rearranges HDD data.
questions.originalExplanation: Encryption uses an algorithm and key to change readable data into ciphertext. It protects privacy; compression reduces size and defragmentation rearranges HDD data.

questions.label: Last lesson — simple
